signals.query: aws logs filter-log-events --region us-west-2 --log-group-name /aws/lambda/immix-autopatrol-schedule-cleanup --filter-pattern 'disabled admin schedule'
signals.description: Count of 'disabled admin schedule' log lines — actual PATCH fires against AutoPatrolSchedule.is_deleted=True. Post-flip (CLEANUP_ENABLED=true, 2026-04-23 17:59Z) this begins firing when a schedule is confirmed gone in Immix. Expected baseline: ~0 initially, small trickle as real stale schedules are caught. Spike >10/h = flap risk, stop and inspect. Manager-visible audit metric.

Schedules that REACHED THRESHOLD but were NOT disabled because Immix reports them as Active/Awaiting. Counted via 'anomaly: bucket=...' log lines. This is the safety-net firing: our connector says the schedule is gone, but Immix says it's live. Elevated rate indicates an ongoing mismatch — either our puller error classifier is wrong OR Immix is reporting stale status OR the schedule is genuinely flapping Active↔Paused. Pairs with actual_disable_rate: if disables=0 but anomaly is high, the safety net is absorbing everything (under-disabling the real stale set). Manager-visible: this quantifies 'Immix-side issues blocking cleanup'.

signals.query: aws logs filter-log-events --region us-west-2 --log-group-name /aws/lambda/immix-autopatrol-schedule-cleanup --start-time $(( $(date -u +%s) * 1000 - 7*86400*1000 )) --filter-pattern 'anomaly: bucket=' --query 'events[].message' --output text | grep -oE 'schedule [a-f0-9-]+' | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 2 {print}' | wc -l
signals.description: Count of DISTINCT schedule_ids that anomaly-reset 2+ times over 7 days. Non-zero means: the connector repeatedly believes a schedule is gone, but Immix repeatedly says active. Classic flappy-schedule / state-mismatch pattern — worth a targeted investigation into that specific schedule's Immix state vs our connector's state. Also surfaces Immix-side flake patterns (same schedule keeps reporting inconsistently). The single-count-unique signal (anomaly_reset_rate) tells you IF there's a problem; this one tells you WHERE to look.
Main-queue depth for the cleanup Lambda's SQS consumer. Healthy = 0..tens during emit bursts. >100 sustained = Lambda lagging behind connector emit rate. Pairs with cleanup_lambda_dlq_depth.

signals.description: Distinct AUTOPATROL connector containers logging the dummy-model fallback warning. >0 means an AutoPatrol site has empty `models` in settings.json and is silently running a no-op model. Use exact-equality match on the message — fleet-wide `LIKE %...%` queries on message time out at NRDB scope.

signals.query: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --granularity DAILY --metrics UnblendedCost (group-by SERVICE, cached aggregate)
signals.description: Total AWS prod-account daily spend. Baseline calibrated 2026-04-30 from 7d trailing: ~$7,788/day (~$234k/mo, ~$2.8M/yr). Sustained drift >25% = a service-level investigation is overdue; check cost_top_services_daily to see which line moved.
signals.would_have_caught: Top-of-funnel drift catcher; would surface anything large enough to move the daily total

signals.query: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --group-by SERVICE (cached aggregate, top-15)
signals.description: Top-15 AWS services by yesterday's spend. FACET dict for sparkline + drift detection per service. Baseline composition 2026-04-30 (7d): EC2 $4663, S3 $1106, DDB $573, EC2-Other $445, ECS $181, RDS $152, VPC $144, AWS Config $129, CloudWatch $93, ELB $71, Glue $51, SQS $44, WAF $32, Lambda $24, ECR $21.
signals.would_have_caught: Service-level cost drift surface. New service appearing in top-15 = unplanned spend; existing service jumping rank = drift.

signals.query: (cached aggregate, key='Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud - Compute')
signals.description: EC2 Compute (BoxUsage) daily. Largest single line item. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $4,663/day. Drift sources: instance-class shift, autoscaling change, missed Savings Plan / RI renewal, new fleet workload.
EC2-Other (NAT, EBS, ELB legacy classic, data transfer). Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $445/day. NAT egress spikes are the usual driver — correlate with VPC endpoint adoption opportunities when red.
DynamoDB daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $573/day. Drift sources: on-demand surge, new table, GSI add, PITR enable.
ECS Fargate daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $181/day. Drift sources: task scale-out, larger task sizes, new service deploy.
RDS daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $152/day. Drift sources: instance upsize, multi-AZ enable, snapshot retention bump, fresh replica.
VPC daily (NAT-Gateway-hours, VPC endpoints). Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $144/day. Drift = NAT GW added or endpoint coverage shifted.

AWS Config recording + rules + delivery channel. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $129/day (~$47k/yr). Surprising line item per /cost-check 2026-04-22 — surface here so any further drift is caught fast. Drift = rules added, recording scope expanded, more resources, or delivery-channel volume up.
CloudWatch daily (logs ingestion + metrics + alarms). Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $93/day. Drift sources: noisy logger added, retention bump, metric explosion (high-cardinality custom metrics).
ELB / ALB / NLB daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $71/day. Drift = new LB created or LCU usage spike (high-throughput connection patterns).
AWS Glue (jobs + crawlers + data catalog). Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $51/day. Drift = added job, larger DPU footprint, more crawler scope.
SQS request volume daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $44/day. Drift = new chatty consumer / producer or polling pattern change.
Lambda daily (invocations + GB-seconds). Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $24/day. Drift sources: provisioned-concurrency add, hot loop, large payload retries.

signals.query: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --filter service=S3 --group-by USAGE_TYPE (cached, classified)
signals.description: S3 USAGE_TYPE-classified breakdown. FACET dict for sparkline. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): tier1_put=$496/day (45%), storage_gb_month=$399/day (36%), tier3_replication=$130/day (12%), tier2_get=$62/day (6%), data_transfer=$18/day (2%). Use this to localize where S3 drift is coming from when cost_s3_daily_total is yellow/red.

S3 Tier3 (replication / lifecycle) daily. The $44k/yr line surfaced 2026-04-22 by /cost-check — replication driver investigation tracked at [[2026-04-23_s3-tier3-cost-investigation]]. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $130/day. Threshold tightened so any new replication policy or lifecycle change spikes here first.
signals.would_have_caught: Open Tier3 investigation (mark-todos §5 pre-PoC item) — would surface any new bucket replication or lifecycle config that moved this number

signals.description: S3 storage GB-month component, daily slice. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $399/day. Slow-changing — drift here = retention policy change or new high-volume writer. Pairs with cost_s3_tier1_daily to distinguish 'more bytes stored' from 'more PUT requests'.

S3 Tier1 (PUT/COPY/POST/LIST request volume) daily. Baseline 2026-04-30 (7d): $496/day — historically the largest S3 line. Heavy frame-write workloads dominate; drift here = ingest pattern shift. Per-unit cost is tiny so this is ~always the volume-driven line.

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(podName) FROM K8sPodSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' AND status='Pending' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Pods stuck in Pending. Non-zero = scheduler can't place / no capacity / image pull stuck / unsatisfiable affinity. Initial threshold 2026-04-27: observed 39 baseline, set conservative thresholds to avoid daily-yellow noise; tighten after 14d of sink data.

signals.nrql: SELECT uniqueCount(nodeName) FROM K8sNodeSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Total node count in the cluster. Drift outside expected range = autoscaler runaway, ghost nodes, capacity drop. Initial calibration 2026-04-27: 110 nodes baseline. Thresholds: yellow if drops below 80 (~25%), red below 50 (~50%); also yellow if exceeds 200 (autoscaler runaway).
signals.would_have_caught: Autoscaler / capacity drift detection

signals.nrql: SELECT sum(deploymentDesiredReplicas - deploymentAvailableReplicas) FROM K8sDeploymentSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Sum of (desired - available) replicas across all deployments. >0 means some deployment can't reach its target replica count — image pull failure, crashloop, anti-affinity stuck, capacity. Brief positive during rolling deploys is normal.
signals.would_have_caught: Deployment stuck-at-replica-N regressions

signals.nrql: SELECT max(restartCount) - min(restartCount) FROM K8sContainerSample WHERE clusterName='Connector-EKS' SINCE 5 minutes ago
signals.description: Restart-count delta over a 5-min window. Fan-out cousin of fleet_oomkills_24h — catches crashloop bursts in real time vs. the 24h aggregate. NB: this is a single max-min across the fleet, not a sum; calibrate after observing real distribution. NRDB has no now() function so the original 'count restarts since now()-5m' formulation didn't work.
signals.would_have_caught: Real-time crashloop detection (5m granularity vs. fleet_oomkills_24h). DISABLED 2026-04-27 pending NRQL design + threshold calibration; see cookbook §Per-source recipes for derivative-based alternatives.

signals.command: python ssl.create_default_context() + getpeercert() per host; days until cert.notAfter
signals.description: Days until each customer-facing HTTPS endpoint's TLS cert expires. FACET dict {host: days_remaining}. Add a host by appending its FQDN to the `hosts` list — the collector iterates and emits one entry per host. Threshold yellow_below=21 (3-week warning), red_below=7 (week-out scramble). Day-1 (2026-04-29): all 4 monitored hosts >100 days. Add more hosts as new endpoints come online (e.g. signal.actuate.ai, customer-specific subdomains). Hosts that fail to connect (DNS / firewall / wrong port) emit null and surface as classification 'error' so you notice the misconfig.
signals.would_have_caught: Customer-facing endpoint cert expiry — first time we get to find out before the customer does.

signals.description: Failed user-systemd units on the minipc. Returns FACET dict {unit_name: 1} so detail page lists exactly WHICH units are failing. Standing alarm — any non-empty result is yellow, multiple is red.

signals.description: Failed system-wide units on the minipc (caddy, docker, tailscaled, etc.). Same shape as the user variant. systemd-networkd-wait-online tends to flap on boot — mask it via phase script if it's the only chronic offender.

FACET dict {repo_name: count}.
signals.would_have_caught: Branch-bloat that would otherwise stay invisible — only the active branches show on /app/repos/.

signals.command: gh run list --limit 50 --json conclusion -R <slug>; pct fail/(fail+ok)
signals.description: Percentage of recent CI workflow runs that ended in failure (last 50 runs). Counts conclusion in {failure, timed_out, startup_failure} as fail; counts {success} as ok. Skipped/cancelled/in-progress are excluded from the denominator. Day-1 distribution (2026-04-29): most repos 0-15%, actuate_ailink the obvious outlier at 38% — broken pipeline. Threshold yellow=10 catches chronic mid-tier debt; red=25 flags actively broken CI. Returns None for repos with no CI runs (drops from FACET).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained CI flake or broken pipeline — would have caught actuate_ailink's 38% rate immediately.

signals.command: gh pr list --state open --limit 50 --json createdAt -R <slug>; median age in days
signals.description: Median age across each repo's currently-open PRs. Pairs with `repo_mtm_days_p50` (merged latency) for a flow picture: high MTM + high open-PR-age = review bottleneck; high MTM + low open-PR-age = recent spike. Repos with zero open PRs drop from the FACET dict (uninteresting / clean). 1 gh API call per repo per collect (16/h, well under rate limit).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained review-bottleneck where PRs queue up days before being looked at.

signals.command: gh pr list --state merged --limit 50 --json mergedAt,createdAt -R <slug>; median delta in days
signals.description: Median time-to-merge across the last 50 merged PRs per repo, in days. Resolves the GitHub slug from each repo's `git config remote.origin.url`. FACET dict {repo_name: float days}. Day-1 baseline (2026-04-29): vms-connector p50 = 0.41 days (~10h). Slow-down indicator: if a team is hitting review or CI-flake bottlenecks, the median creeps up. Fast-down indicator: a flurry of stage-bot autobumps drops the median; that's healthy noise. 1 gh API call per repo per collect (7/h, well under 5000/h limit).
signals.would_have_caught: Sustained CI flake or review-bottleneck regression — visible as p50 climbing over 7d.

signals.description: Likely-unused functions, classes, vars per repo at >=80% vulture confidence. The default 60% bucket is dominated by Django framework FPs (Meta classes, migrations, apps.py, model field declarations, enum members) — see [[2026-04-29_minipc-api-surface]] / collect.py for the FP-cut analysis. Bumping to 80% drops actuate_admin from 3308 to 41 (98% noise reduction) while preserving rank order across all 16 repos. Day-1 baselines (2026-04-29 conf80): connector_deployer=45, actuate-libraries=45, actuate_admin=41, vms-connector=34, actuate-watchman=22, queue_consumer=11, actuate_ailink=8, autopatrol-server=8, autopatrol_onboarder=6, actuate_monitoring_api=6, ds-terraform-eks-v2=3, others=0-2. Thresholds set at ~2x current top-of-set so a real refactor regression flags but normal scale doesn't.
signals.would_have_caught: Dead-code accrual after a refactor — flagged via baseline_drift on next collect.

signals.query: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --granularity DAILY --metrics UnblendedCost --filter service=S3
signals.description: Total S3 daily spend across the prod account. Baseline calibrated 2026-04-30 from 7d trailing: ~$1106/day avg (~$33k/mo). Sustained jumps >30% indicate new lifecycle rule gone wrong, sudden replication, or retention change. See cost_s3_breakdown_daily for the Tier1/2/3/Storage decomposition.
signals.would_have_caught: Baseline surface for Tier-3 S3 investigations (see 2026-04-23_s3-tier3-cost-investigation)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='queue-eagle-eye-consumer' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for queue-eagle-eye-consumer. Alert-pipeline health signal — catches 'consumer silently stopped processing'. Thresholds calibrated 2026-04-24 against 7d data (14 buckets, median 3910, min 781, max 15436).
signals.would_have_caught: Future eagle-eye consumer outage; analog of the 2026-04-23 onboarder silent-early-return pattern

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='queue-evalink-consumer' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for queue-evalink-consumer. Companion to queue_evalink_errors_12h — catches silent-drop that error-count can miss. Thresholds calibrated 2026-04-24 against 7d data (median 1925, min 1006, max 5238).

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='frontel-puller' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for frontel-puller. Frontel VMS integration puller. Thresholds calibrated 2026-04-24 against 7d data (median 195, min 119, max 341).

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='clips-smtp-worker' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for clips-smtp-worker. Low-volume service (median 44 over 7d). A 0-bucket is not unusual; 2+ consecutive zeros should be. Thresholds intentionally generous — real concern is 0 for extended period.

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='smtp-frame-receiver' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for smtp-frame-receiver. High-throughput service (7d median ~22.7M). Static thresholds uninformative; silent_drop rule catches 'stopped processing' (value < 10% of prior-day).

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='clips-prod' SINCE 12 hours ago
signals.description: Total log volume for clips-prod. High-throughput service with clear day/night bimodal pattern (7d range 8.5M-24.6M). Silent-drop rule catches stopping entirely; baseline_drift will catch pattern shift.

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND (message LIKE '%AccessDeniedException%' OR message LIKE '%is not authorized to perform%' OR message LIKE '%not authorized to perform%') FACET container_name SINCE 12 hours ago LIMIT 10
signals.description: Cluster-wide IAM AccessDenied detector. Counts AccessDeniedException + 'not authorized to perform' message patterns across all Connector-EKS containers, faceted by container. IAM denials are NEVER a normal steady state — any non-zero count means a service is missing a permission grant (new GSI, new resource, role drift). Caught the 2026-04-29 autopatrol-microservice-role MotionFrame/index/run_timestamp gap retroactively; a yellow_above=1 threshold means the next instance flags within 12h instead of waiting for a manual overnight check.
signals.would_have_caught: 2026-04-29 autopatrol-microservice-role MotionFrame GSI denial (~27 hits in 12h before fix; would have flagged on first hit)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND message LIKE '%site_product_ended%' AND container_name LIKE '%vch%' SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: VCH billing events (site_product_ended) emitted in 6h. Each VCH cronjob run emits one event per camera healthchecked; ~870/6h Saturday peak, ~250/6h Sunday low (2026-05-03). PR #1667 (2026-05-02) fixed the SIGTERM-loss regression that silently dropped all billing on interrupt. 38/38 SIGTERM'd pods verified emitting post-fix vs 0/N pre-fix. silent_drop_inverse against 7d baseline is primary detector once history accumulates; absolute thresholds below are near-zero floors.
signals.would_have_caught: Pre-2026-05-02 silent SIGTERM-induced VCH billing-event loss (issue #1666)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND message LIKE '%site_product_ended%' AND container_name LIKE '%-chm-cronjob%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%vch%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%autopatrol%' SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: CHM (regular healthcheck) billing events emitted in 6h. Highest-volume integration class — ~31K/6h baseline (~780 pods, ~40 events/pod = ~40 cameras/run). CHM has no SIGTERM handler today; same lifecycle-invariant bug class would manifest as a flat drop in this signal. silent_drop_inverse catches relative drops; absolute floors below trigger only on near-total emission failure.
signals.would_have_caught: Future CHM billing-emit regressions analogous to the VCH SIGTERM bug (issue #1666)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND message LIKE '%site_product_ended%' AND container_name LIKE '%autopatrol%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%vch%' SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: AutoPatrol (non-VCH) billing events emitted in 6h. Low-volume class — ~360/6h baseline. PR #1663 (2026-05-01) fixed an emit gap in AutoPatrolSiteManager / PatrolSiteManager that had been silent for ~6 months. silent_drop_inverse against 7d baseline is the primary detector. Absolute red floor of 1 triggers only on full-zero (no AP runs in 6h).
signals.would_have_caught: PR #1663-class regressions in AutoPatrol/Patrol manager emit paths

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND message LIKE '%site_product_ended%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%vch%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%-chm-cronjob%' AND container_name NOT LIKE '%autopatrol%' SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: Analytics (long-running site-manager) billing events emitted in 6h. Largest-volume class — ~140K/6h baseline (~7400 pods including both connector-NNNN and named-client containers like 'five-star-medical-XXXX'). Catches regressions in AnalyticsSiteManager.endrun and ChunkedSiteManager.endrun.
signals.would_have_caught: Future emit regressions in Analytics/Chunked site managers (analogous code paths to PR #1663 patrol-manager fix)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND message LIKE '%site_product_ended%' SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: Fleet-wide site_product_ended emit count across all integration classes (VCH + CHM + AutoPatrol + Analytics) in 6h. Top-level sanity check — ~180K/6h baseline. A coordinated drop here means something fleet-wide is wrong (event-handler ELB down, SQS issue, internal-event-handler outage). Per-class signals identify which integration regressed; this one says 'something is broken everywhere.'
signals.would_have_caught: Fleet-wide event-handler / SQS / ELB outages affecting billing

signals.description: Count of image-backed Lambdas whose currently-deployed digest would be pruned at the next ECR lifecycle policy evaluation. Should always be 0. Any non-zero means we are one cold-start / scale-up event away from an inference-style outage. Audit walks us-west-2/us-east-1/eu-west-1, simulates each repo's lifecycle rules against the live image set + digest used by Code.ImageUri.
signals.would_have_caught: 2026-05-02 InferenceAPI-prod outage (ECR lifecycle pruned the live image's digest)

signals.description: FACET dict of ECR repos with overly-broad lifecycle expire rules — tagPatternList=['.*'] / '*' / [] applied to tagged images. These rules will eventually prune in-use images even if no Lambda is at risk *today*. Companion to ecr_pruning_risk_count: this catches the bug when the repo has few images, before count crosses the rule's threshold. Yellow if any exists, red if any deployed digest is also at risk.
signals.would_have_caught: Class of ECR-lifecycle policy errors that took down inference 2026-05-02

signals.query: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/Lambda --metric-name Errors --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=InferenceAPI-prod --region us-west-2 --period 3600 --statistics Sum
signals.description: InferenceAPI-prod Lambda function-level Errors metric over the last hour, in us-west-2. Reactive companion to ecr_pruning_risk_count: catches anything that spikes Lambda errors — image-pull failures, unhandled exceptions, OOMs, init-time crashes. The 2026-05-02 outage drove this to thousands/hour for hours; we want to learn that within the next dashboard tick (≤1h) instead.
signals.would_have_caught: 2026-05-02 InferenceAPI-prod outage (caught the 5XX spike in real time)

signals.query: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/Lambda --metric-name Errors --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=InferenceAPI-prod --region eu-west-1 --period 3600 --statistics Sum
signals.description: Same as inferenceapi_prod_errors_us_west_2 but for the EU region. Independent dimension so a single-region incident is visible without being averaged against a healthy region.
signals.would_have_caught: Future eu-west-1-only inference outage

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name LIKE 'autopatrol-server%' AND message LIKE '%Generating patrol summary%' SINCE 1 hour ago
signals.description: Count of 'Generating patrol summary' lines emitted by autopatrol-server containers in the last hour. Each line corresponds to one patrol going through the summarizer; rate-of-zero is the silent-break detector (the autopatrol equivalent of the 2026-04-23 onboarder incident). Note: NR k8s integration tags clusterName='Connector-EKS' even though the AWS cluster is inference-eks-Ny9n. Wildcard on container_name covers both 'autopatrol-server-dev' (~14.8k logs/24h, the active container) and 'autopatrol-server' (~58 logs/24h, legacy/secondary). Original signal used exact-match container_name='autopatrol-server' which never matched the active container — surfaced + fixed 2026-05-15 (4-day false-RED).
signals.would_have_caught: Future autopatrol-server silent-break (analog of 2026-04-23 onboarder incident)

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='autopatrol-server' AND (level='ERROR' OR message LIKE '% - ERROR - %') SINCE 1 hour ago
signals.description: Error-level log line count for the autopatrol-server prod container. Catches structured logs (level='ERROR') AND text-format logs (message matching the ' - ERROR - ' segment from the stdlib basicConfig prefix '<ts> - <logger> - ERROR - <body>'). The dual match means the signal works today and stays correct after structured logging ships (see autopatrol-server NR upgrade workstream). Calibrated empirically: 24h window 2026-05-04 had 0 errors, so threshold yellow>5 / red>20 errors-per-hour is a generous spike detector that won't false-positive on noise.
signals.would_have_caught: Spike in summarizer / handler exceptions

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name='autopatrol-server' AND (message LIKE '%Unable to connect to cameras during this patrol%' OR message LIKE '%could not be reached%') SINCE 1 hour ago
signals.description: Count of patrols that hit the new connection-failure summary path (PR #26, 2026-05-04). A non-trivial trickle is normal — connection failures happen. A sudden spike means something upstream broke (camera fleet down, immix outage, connector crash). Also serves as the deploy-acceptance-test for the fix: once we see the first non-zero count, we have proof the new code path renders correctly in prod.
signals.would_have_caught: Camera fleet connectivity degradation

signals.description: Production cameras (not trial/internal) running billable products but NOT in usage_monthly. Sourced from daily billing-reconcile-check timer (post-SPRD-swap). May 2026 actual: 2,024 cams; Feb 2026 baseline: 803 cams. Stale-file alarm covered by billing_reconcile_freshness.
signals.would_have_caught: Cohort F missing-subscription class (~400 of the 642 cams)

signals.description: Reconciliation residual — every Postgres-active camera should land in exactly one pipeline bucket (Connector / Clip / VCH). Non-zero indicates a counting bug, schema drift, or unhandled integration type. Default 999 if JSON missing (covers stale-file case).
signals.would_have_caught: Counting drift in reconcile_cameras.py if a new integration type lands without script update

signals.description: Count of reconciliation JSON sinks written in the last 24h. Expected: 1. Zero means the systemd timer didn’t fire or the wrapper exited before writing. Catches missing daily runs that would otherwise leave the other two billing signals reading stale numbers.
signals.would_have_caught: Timer wedge / wrapper regression / sink-dir permission loss

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE cluster_name='Connector-EKS' AND container_name NOT LIKE 'staging-%' AND (message LIKE '%empty_metrics_dict%' OR message LIKE '%no products configured%') SINCE 6 hours ago
signals.description: AP/VCH schedule pods where billing-emit got an empty plain_metrics dict for at least one stream. Two log tokens covered: the new connector-side WARN ('empty_metrics_dict', fires at HttpOnlyAdminDAO.get_product_by_metrics — earliest detection) and the downstream misconfigured-fallback WARN ('no products configured', fires from billing_emit). Expected steady-state: 0 once admin-side generator bug is fixed. Discovered 2026-05-21 via NR log triage for connector-46767-autopatrol-1102; root cause is actuate_admin commit 627af2c2 (Dec 2025) emitting empty metrics when schedule_product_metrics doesn't intersect with stream.stream_metrics. Currently ~180/6h pre-fix (sites 37837, 41070, 46767).
signals.would_have_caught: 2026-05-21 ap-empty-metrics class — schedule settings.json generated with empty metrics → connector falls back to 'misconfigured' billing product silently

signals.nrql: SELECT count(*) FROM Log WHERE container_name = 'prod_camera_admin' AND message LIKE '%ap_metrics_fallback_all%' SINCE 24 hours ago
signals.description: Upstream pair to ap_empty_metrics_warn_6h. Fires from actuate_admin's SettingsGenerator.list_metrics_by_schedule when an AP schedule's schedule_product_metrics(enabled=True) doesn't intersect with the camera stream's stream_metrics — the generator falls back to stream.stream_metrics.all() instead of writing empty metrics to S3, so the connector keeps working but the data inconsistency surfaces here. Each event identifies a (stream, schedule) pair that needs admin-side cleanup (either populate the schedule's product metrics or adjust the stream's metric assignments).
signals.would_have_caught: Same as ap_empty_metrics_warn_6h but caught at the admin generator one step earlier — settings are never uploaded broken
